summary: TKT-88 follow-up: kimi-k3 re-review clarity nits (test-only)

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
Follow-up to TKT-88, **risk:low** (test-only comment/fixture cleanup, no product code, isolated to two smoke files).

**Origin:** the repo owner asked to re-run the TKT-88 code review with `kimi-k3@claudex` now that the provider is healthy (it was down during TKT-88, which ran on the gpt-5.6-sol fallback). kimi's re-review returned **verdict: approve** with 5 non-blocking clarity/robustness nits. The owner directed fixing all 5.

**Gateless** (owner-directed cleanup): same waiver posture as TKT-88 — agent carries it through to merge.

**risk:low rationale:** test-only, 2 files, 4 of 5 changes are pure comments/constants, the 5th (F1) turned out to be a documentation fix (see below). Well under the >5-files / auth / money / migration / CI thresholds.

<!-- sdlc:stage=coding kind=summary -->
Implemented by main-agent. The 5 kimi nits:

- **F1 (pass-test exit fixture)** — kimi flagged the withdrawing exit's claimed time (`+8m`) sits between the two entries rather than after both. **Investigated: this is NOT a nit to "fix" by moving the time.** `DerivePolicyConflicts` (conflicts.go) walks facts by claimed time and raises `exit_required` for an entry landing while-inside; moving the exit to `+25m` (after the reconciled `+20m` entry) leaves that entry landing while-inside, so the conflict CORRECTLY stays raised — the withdrawal is a property of the timeline, not of "an exit." The gate caught my first (wrong) fix. Final change: kept `+8m` (the withdrawing timeline) and replaced the comment with an accurate explanation of the ordering-dependence. **kimi's finding was valuable — it surfaced a real non-obvious semantic, just not the fix it implied.**
- **F2** — comment on `alarmEnvelopesFor`'s `ORDER BY created_at` (insertion order, not an authoritative sequence).
- **F3** — comment on `assertRedeemedOccurrence` that isolation comes from the fresh ticket id, not DB partitioning.
- **F4** — named constant `wantSingleEntryTickets = 2` + comment tying it to `reserveCheckout`'s quantity, so a future fixture change surfaces clearly.
- **F5** — comment on the replay `ScannedAt.Equal` precision-coupling (safe: microsecond truncation both sides).

Net: comments + one constant + one accurate comment rewrite. No behavior change (F1's behavior is identical to TKT-88 as merged). `make check` green (verify-lifecycle passes).

<!-- sdlc:stage=done kind=metrics -->
**TKT-100 closed — DONE.** Merged to `main` @ 5e88816 (PR #77). risk:low, gateless (owner-directed cleanup).

## Metrics
| stage | duration |
|---|---|
| Building (create → merge) | ~35m — 5 nit edits, 2 `make check` runs (1 caught a wrong F1 fix), PR, CI, merge |
| human-wait | 0 (risk:low skips Gate 2; owner directed the rest) |

**diff:** +34 / −5 (2 files, test-only).

## Why this ticket existed
The owner re-ran the TKT-88 code review with the configured reviewer `kimi-k3@claudex` (TKT-88 had run on the gpt-5.6-sol fallback because kimi was down). kimi returned **approve, 0 blocking, 5 clarity nits**; the owner directed fixing all 5.

## The one that mattered (F1)
kimi flagged the pass-flow withdrawal fixture's exit time as "mid-timeline." **Acting on it surfaced a real, non-obvious semantic, not a cosmetic fix:** `DerivePolicyConflicts` walks facts by claimed time, so whether a live exit *withdraws* the reconciliation-raised `exit_required` depends on where the exit sorts relative to the reconciled entry. My first fix (moving the exit to +25m) made the gate FAIL — because at +25m the reconciled entry still lands while-inside and the conflict CORRECTLY stays raised. Reverted to +8m (the withdrawing timeline) with an accurate comment documenting the dependence. **No behavior change from TKT-88 as merged** — the merged fixture always exercised the correct case; only the comment was misleading, and now isn't.

## learnings
- **A re-review by the config's intended model is worth running even post-merge.** kimi (the configured `aiReview`) agreed with the gpt-5.6-sol fallback on all substantive semantics — a useful cross-model confirmation that the fallback didn't miss anything — AND its one "nit" exposed a genuine ordering-dependence in the derived-conflict projection worth documenting. Target house: the value is captured in this thread + the code comment; no ADR/skill change needed (the semantic is in `conflicts.go:orderFacts` + `DerivePolicyConflicts`, discoverable).
- **kimi-k3@claudex works again** (the TKT-88 outage was transient). No config change needed.

## retro
**(1) What would have made this faster/better?** I initially treated kimi's Finding 1 as a fixture-time tweak and made a wrong change that the gate caught. Reading `DerivePolicyConflicts` BEFORE editing (not after the failure) would have shown the ordering-dependence up front and gone straight to the comment fix. *Concrete:* when a review finding touches a fixture whose values feed a derived/ordered projection, trace the projection's ordering rule before changing the values. This is judgment, not a skill rule — noted here, not patched.
**(2) What should the humans change?** Nothing. The gateless-with-gate-verification flow behaved correctly: my wrong fix was caught by `make check`, not shipped. The one open item from TKT-88 remains: optionally add a *generation* probe to the claudex-runner pre-flight so a dead provider fails fast instead of hanging a full stage timeout (offered to the owner; not applied).
